text: Hello everyone, welcome back.In the previous lesson, we have learned about the generally accepted scientific explanations for human's perception of taste by reading the article A Question of Taste.Today, in the second period, we'll continue to have a deep understanding of the article.By the end of this period, you are expected to explain people's taste preferences and reactions by associating it with the scientific explanations introduced in the previous passage and also to design the experiment procedures to prove your claims while explaining the reasons behind the test results.Before class, please get your textbook and worksheets ready.Recently, I came across a Chinese idiom, though lamb may be good, it is difficult to cook it to suit everyone's taste.According to what we've learned in the previous lesson, what is the idea behind the idiom?Please think about it.You will have one minute to prepare.Steve has something to say.According to the generally accepted scientific explanations in the previous lesson, personal perception of taste is actually an individual experience.Human beings' senses of sight, smell, touch, and taste all have a role to play, and they work together to contribute to our perception of taste.Thank you.I totally agree with you.And I suppose we can explain certain phenomena in life by associating it with scientific ideas introduced in the passage.So it is with the phenomena in life in the following deep reading section.Please check the exercise on page 63.Study the following statements about people's taste preferences and reactions.Find reasons in the passage to support each statement.The first one is an example to follow.Statement one.When people grow older, they sometimes start to like certain vegetables which they disliked before.The statement provides me with food for thought.Why people's taste preferences change as they age?Apparently, we can apply the theory introduced in the first paragraph to this phenomenon.The reason is young people's taste buds are not fully developed.So they find it hard to accept the bitter taste of some vegetables.When they grow older, they may find it easier to do so.Now it's your turn.You will have five minutes to think about the following five phenomena.Statement 2Most people feel happy when eating dessert.What contributes to most people's preference for a sweet taste?Are there any historical reasons?Humans began to associate a sweet taste with health and nutrition long ago.Our prehistoric ancestors ate a lot of sweet, ripe fruit because it was widely available and easy to notice on trees, and it was a good source of energy.They realized that eating sweet tasting food would make them feel comfortable and strong.That's why most people feel happy when eating dessert.Statement 3People naturally dislike bitter flavor.If people accidentally had a bitter taste of food, what would they relate it to?Sayings with a bitter taste were often poisonous.So humans tend to associate a bitter taste with discomfort.That's why we naturally dislike such tastes.Statement 4Cooked food often tastes better than raw food.Then what happens to the food when it is cooked?This shows the importance of smell in the perception of taste.When food is cooked, it produces aromas so that people find the food tastier.Raw food doesn't give the same kind of aroma.Statement 5Some people can't stand the thought of eating snails.How do these people feel?The texture of food will influence people's perception of its taste.Snails look ugly and unpleasant to some people.So they refuse to eat them.Statement 6People like beautifully displayed dishes.Statement 6People like beautifully displayed dishes because these dishes often look very appealing.How does the sense of sight affect our perception of taste?The look or feel of something also helps people perceive taste.Beautifully displayed dishes look more pleasant.When our brain receives the feeling of beautiful things,it sends a message to our tongue, telling it to like that food.That is why we may have a stronger desire to taste beautifully displayed dishes.Scientists firmly believe that all the scientific explanations or reasons must be inferred from carefully designed experiments.The mini project today is for us to design experiments to test claims.The passage gives some suggestions on the kind of experiment we can do to test certain claims.You are going to design some similar experiments to test claim 2 and claim 3 in a table.Discussing groups and answer the questions.What is your experiment design?Why did you design the experiment?Select one person to report on behalf of your group.Please remember this is the group work.So we need one organizer, one secretary and one reporter on behalf of your group.Let's take claim 1 as an example.Claim 1.Our taste buds and noses work together to decide what flavor the food has.The procedures and the result of the experiment go like this.Close your eyes and pinch your nose between your fingers.Then ask someone to put a small piece of food in your mouth and try to identify it.Repeat the experiment several times.You will find it somewhat difficult to do that.The reason behind is that flavor is a combination of many factors, including taste and smell.Without smell, it can be hard to identify what food it is.Now, please pay careful attention to the structure and the writing techniques of the report above.When it comes to designing an experiment, please be aware that1.Your report should include claims, procedures, results and reasons of the experiment.The procedures can be described in imperative sentences.The procedures should follow the order of how the experiment is conducted.The results and reasons should stick to what you have observed in the experiment.Next, let's have a try.Girls and boys perceive taste differently.Please follow the above instructions.You will be given two minutes to prepare and then give a report.Simon, please share your group idea with others.My experiment goes like this.Ask a group of girls and boys to taste the flavor of several drinks with different concentration levels of sugar.Girls will probably be able to distinguish the sweet flavor faster than boys, even when the concentration of sugar in the drinks is very low.The reason is that girls have more sensitive taste buds and can taste flavors more easily, like sweet and sour.Good, your experiment is well organized and effective.The texture of food on our tongue is important in our perception of its taste.Girls will probably be given two minutes to prepare and then give a report.
